title: DAIRY CATTLE BREEDING
text:
DAIRY CATTLE BREEDING

Objectives:
1. To know the definition and purpose of breeding dairy cattle
2. To familiarize the different breeding system

Breeding - the mating and production of offspring by animals.

Breeding system:
1. Natural breeding - mating of animals by natural means.
2. Artificial breeding - is done through artificial means by collecting semen from male and inseminating the females using an AI gun.

[Photo: Natural breeding]
Natural breeding

[Photo: Artificial insemination]
Artificial insemination

Natural breeding vs. Artificial breeding:
| Feature | Natural breeding | Artificial breeding |
|---|---|---|
| Heat detection | • Reduces the need of detecting heat detection.
• Bulls will detect the cows in heat. | • Requires skilful personnel on heat detection.
• Cows in heat must be detected in order to be inseminated. |
| Bull maintenance | • Need to invest in bull maintenance | • Does not need a bull |
| Breeding Facility | • Low cost breeding facility | • High cost breeding facility, especially in semen storage and examination. |
| Breeding related injuries | • High risk especially in bigger bulls bred to small cows. | • Very low risk |
| Transmission of venereal disease | • Very high due to direct contact during mating. | • Very low risk, bull's semen is strictly evaluated. Bulls undergo screening and tests. |
| Semen quality | • Is not checked | • Semen motility and concentration. |
| Breeding record | • Difficult to monitor | • Easy monitoring |

facts: Breeding is defined as the mating and production of offspring by animals.
The objectives of the module are to know the definition and purpose of breeding dairy cattle, and to familiarize the different breeding systems.
Natural breeding is the mating of animals by natural means.
Artificial breeding is done through artificial means by collecting semen from the male and inseminating the females using an AI gun.
In natural breeding, bulls detect cows in heat, reducing the need for human heat detection.
In artificial breeding, skilful personnel are required for heat detection, and cows in heat must be detected in order to be inseminated.
Natural breeding requires investment in bull maintenance, whereas artificial breeding does not need a bull on the farm.
Natural breeding utilizes a low cost breeding facility.
Artificial breeding requires a high cost breeding facility, especially for semen storage and examination.
Breeding-related injuries carry a high risk in natural breeding, particularly when bigger bulls are bred to small cows.
Breeding-related injuries have a very low risk in artificial breeding.
Transmission of venereal disease is very high in natural breeding due to direct contact during mating.
Transmission of venereal disease is very low risk in artificial breeding because the bull's semen is strictly evaluated and bulls undergo screening and tests.
Semen quality is not checked in natural breeding.
In artificial breeding, semen quality is evaluated for semen motility and concentration.
Breeding records are difficult to monitor in natural breeding but easy to monitor in artificial breeding.
